The Office of Safety Standards (OSS) Document Control System (OSS DCS), is the primary project management tool OSS executives, managers, and employees use to coordinate memorandums and letters for grid and signature coordination, and to monitor and track projects – including: Congressional inquiries, draft legislation, NTSB and FAA Safety Recommendations, petitions for rulemaking and exemptions, requests from air carriers and operators across the National Airspace System, requests for technical support from FAA Flight Standards Offices across the nation, ICAO document reviews and briefings, civil aviation authority inquiries from around the world, and to manage and process revisions to orders, advisory circulars, Information for Operators, Safety Alerts for Operators, notices, FAA Order 8900.1 and other Orders.

This system provides reporting functionality so managers and their team members can effectively monitor suspense dates, track, and prioritize work within the OSS, and it provides essential data FAA managers use to quantify staffing and funding resource allocations.

The system also provides links to project folders so all documentation associated with a given project can be stored during the pre-decision phase (Note: after a final decision is made signed documents are moved to a shared drive that is approved for records management storage and retention purposes), and the system provides managers and team members with automated email notifications when project status changes.

This essential tool directly supports the FAA’s efforts to efficiently promote commerce within the US, and to coordinate and collaborate with global partners around the world.
New discovery in FY26 - verified with POCs
